description:
Perform a Three-Point Resection (Snellius-Pothenot problem) in GeoGebra to determine the coordinates of your station point P. You are given three known landmarks with local grid coordinates (in meters): A=(-300, 200), B=(100, 500), and C=(400, -100). From point P, you measure the horizontal angle between A and B as 40 degrees, and the angle between B and C as 70 degrees. Point P is located south of the landmarks. 

Construct the solution geometrically using the 'Circle of Position' method (finding the intersection of two loci circles). 

Steps:
1. Plot points A, B, and C.
2. Construct the two circular loci corresponding to the measured angles (hint: use the inscribed angle theorem properties or the 'Circle through 3 Points' tool if you construct the apex).
3. Mark the intersection point P.
4. Verify your result by creating segments PA, PB, PC and measuring angles APB and BPC.
5. Save your construction as 'resection_solution.ggb' in ~/Documents/GeoGebra/projects/.
